project.name: neo-deep-agent-lab
project.description: A conversational SQL agent with sandboxed execution via Modal, hybrid BM25+vector recall via ParadeDB, a 7-layer middleware stack, and a React/TypeScript frontend with SSE streaming.

layers.name: API & Server Layer
layers.description: FastAPI application entry point, REST/SSE endpoints, authentication, session management, log streaming, SSE event encoding, and CLI interface. Orchestrates agent invocations and exposes all backend capabilities over HTTP.

layers.name: Agent & Middleware Layer
layers.description: LangGraph agent factory, system prompt engineering, and the middleware stack (context injection, schema caching, SQL guard, logging). Assembles the AI agent with tools, middleware, and HITL configuration.

layers.name: Tools Layer
layers.description: LangChain tool implementations for SQL execution, schema introspection, data analysis, chart generation, CSV/JSON export, context persistence, and scratchpad notes. Includes Pydantic input schemas and shared sandbox helpers.

layers.name: Data & Sandbox Layer
layers.description: PostgreSQL persistence (checkpointing, long-term memory, BM25 indexing), Modal sandbox lifecycle (image building, snapshot management, psql gateway), RAG pipeline (parsing, chunking, embedding, vector storage), and sandbox scripts for analysis/charting.

layers.name: Frontend Layer
layers.description: React/TypeScript SPA with Zustand state management, SSE streaming client, API utilities, and UI components for chat, context inspection, document management, HITL approval, agent management, and provider selection.

layers.name: Legacy Frontend Layer
layers.description: Vanilla JavaScript SPA served as static files. Includes DOM builders for chat, context panel, and HITL modal; service modules for API, chat SSE, context, HITL, and provider management; plus utility functions for markdown rendering and SSE parsing.

layers.name: Infrastructure & Support Layer
layers.description: Cross-cutting concerns: application configuration (Pydantic settings), constants/enums, centralized logging with metrics, database migrations (Alembic), Git hooks, DevOps scripts, package init files, and the test suite.

tour.title: FastAPI Entry Point
tour.description: The server starts here. src/server/app.py is the central hub with 14 outgoing dependencies — it wires together the agent, persistence, streaming, and session layers. Understanding this file reveals the entire application skeleton.
tour.languageLesson: Pydantic Settings for configuration: the config module uses BaseSettings with environment variable binding, a common FastAPI pattern for 12-factor app compliance.

tour.title: Agent Factory
tour.description: From the server, requests flow into the agent factory. src/agent/factory.py has the highest fan-out in the project (14 edges) — it assembles the LangGraph agent by composing tools, middleware, prompts, and HITL configuration. This is where the AI brain gets built.
tour.languageLesson: LangGraph's create_react_agent pattern with a middleware stack: the factory injects middleware as a composable pipeline, demonstrating Python's higher-order function capabilities.

tour.title: Context Engineering
tour.description: The agent needs memory. This cluster handles hybrid BM25+vector recall via ParadeDB, context persistence, and thread-scoped variables. The context store is the 4th most depended-upon module (10 fan-in), tightly coupled with session management.
tour.languageLesson: Python contextvars for thread-local state: thread_var.py uses contextvars.ContextVar to pass request-scoped data without explicit parameter threading.

tour.title: Middleware Stack
tour.description: Between the agent and its tools sits a 7-layer middleware stack. Context injection enriches each request with recalled memories, the SQL guard validates queries, and the schema cache avoids redundant introspection. These middleware modules connect the context layer (step 3) to the tools layer (step 5).

tour.title: Tool Implementations
tour.description: The agent acts through tools. SQL execution, chart generation, CSV/JSON export, schema introspection, and a scratchpad for working notes. Each tool follows a consistent pattern: Pydantic input schema, sandbox delegation, and structured output. The tools layer is the workhorse that the middleware stack protects.
tour.languageLesson: LangChain's @tool decorator with Pydantic args_schema: each tool declares a typed input model, enabling automatic validation and documentation generation.

tour.title: Modal Sandbox
tour.description: SQL queries do not run locally — they execute inside ephemeral Modal sandboxes with isolated PostgreSQL instances. The sandbox module manages image building, snapshot lifecycle, and a psql gateway. This isolation is what makes the agent safe for arbitrary SQL execution.
tour.languageLesson: Modal's @app.function decorator for serverless GPU/CPU functions: the sandbox uses Modal's container lifecycle to spin up ephemeral PostgreSQL instances on demand.

tour.title: Streaming & SSE
tour.description: Results stream back to the client via Server-Sent Events. The SSE encoder serializes agent events (tool calls, tokens, errors) into a typed event protocol. This layer connects the agent's async output (from steps 2-6) to the frontend (steps 9-10).

tour.title: Persistence Layer
tour.description: Long-term state lives in PostgreSQL. The persistence module provides LangGraph checkpointing and memory storage, while Alembic manages schema migrations. The context store from step 3 depends on this layer for durable hybrid-search indexing.

tour.title: RAG Pipeline
tour.description: Documents uploaded by users flow through a parsing, chunking, embedding, and vector storage pipeline. The RAG router exposes upload/query endpoints at the API layer (step 1), and retrieved chunks feed into the context store (step 3) for agent recall.

tour.title: React Frontend
tour.description: The TypeScript SPA consumes the SSE stream and REST API. Zustand stores manage chat, session, HITL, and context state. The frontend types module is the 3rd most depended-upon node (11 fan-in), serving as the shared contract between all UI components.
tour.languageLesson: Zustand's create() with TypeScript generics: each store is a typed slice of global state, avoiding Redux boilerplate while maintaining type safety across the SSE event protocol.

tour.title: Frontend Components
tour.description: UI components consume the Zustand stores. The chat panel renders streamed messages, the HITL modal gates dangerous tool calls for human approval, and the context sidebar exposes the agent's memory. These components complete the user-facing loop that started at the server entry point in step 1.

tour.title: Tests & Infrastructure
tour.description: The test suite validates the middleware stack, streaming protocol, SQL guard, session management, and tool contracts. conftest.py provides shared fixtures including mock sandboxes and test databases. These tests document the expected behavior of every layer visited in the tour.
